$comment: AgentOracle v0.3 recommendation_rules conformance vectors. Drafted 2026-08-27. NOT NORMATIVE until reviewed and published. Pins mapping-agentoracle-v0.3-2026-05-30 recommendation_rules + gate_map against regression. Each vector asserts the DERIVATION (v_verdict, v_adversarial_result, v_confidence) -> (v_recommendation, verdict). Signatures are deliberately out of scope: these test the rule table, not the signer.
gate_map: only confident_supported -> act; all else -> halt

vectors.why: The service-integrity self-contradiction case. A supported verdict with the adversarial dimension NOT evaluated is a legitimate, named state. It must be labelled un_probed_not_cleared and must halt. This is the vector the 2026-08-25 incident was filed against; the receipt layer already satisfied it.

A receipt asserting a pass decision while the adversarial dimension reads not_checked. This is the artifact that MUST fail the build. If this vector ever passes, supported-under-not_checked has become reachable as act and the gate_map has been broken.

Guards the OTHER direction, which is how we broke it ourselves on 2026-08-27. Routing non-evaluation to unknown makes the rule table exit at rule 6 and emit the generic unverifiable, destroying the distinction between 'no attempt was made' (un_probed_not_cleared) and 'an attempt failed' (unverifiable). Both halt, so a decision-only test does not catch this. wg-identity#21: indeterminate and not-evaluated must not collapse.
The only path to act. Proves the accept vector above is not passing merely because everything halts.
Same not_checked adversarial state, below threshold. Must be distinguishable from rule 2 - confidence and non-evaluation are independent axes.
Adversarial ran and found a contradiction. Distinct from both not_checked states.
A genuine failed attempt to establish the claim. Shares the halt decision with rule 2 but MUST carry a different recommendation - that difference is the whole point.

vectors.designation: SERVICE INTEGRITY / NOT A GATE VECTOR
vectors.why: Records the D1 requirement, which the rule table cannot express because it is about whether a receipt is issued at all. A zero-member evaluation MUST NOT produce a signed receipt in any state. Asserted by the runner as an absence, not a derivation.
